news.title: Just nine countries back pledge to tackle AI’s environmental footprint
paras: Nine countries signed a pledge at the COP31 climate summit to make artificial intelligence (AI) greener. The pledge encourages cleaner energy for AI, improves efficiency of computer centres, and asks companies to reveal AI’s environmental impact. It matters because AI uses a lot of electricity, which can hurt climate goals.

AI’s rapid growth is putting pressure on power grids. Even firms that invest in renewable energy, like Amazon and Google, sometimes use fossil fuels to keep up. A researcher, Ketan Joshi, says there is little proof that enough clean power is built to meet AI’s demands. The pledge is voluntary, so it does not force countries to cut emissions or energy use.

news.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
paras: A privacy win (mostly) Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data AI training and chat history will now have separate toggles in the Gemini activity settings. That is, of course, by design .

The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app. The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data.

paras: "Early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance." The launch ended up failing, and the satellites were lost.

news.title: On this day in space! Nov. 17, 1967: NASA's Surveyor 6 moon probe makes 1st-ever successful launch and hop fro
paras: Surveyor 6 showed that spacecraft could land on the moon, and lift off again. The lives of NASA's Apollo astronauts depended on it. 17, 1967, NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft made the first liftoff from the lunar surface.

Surveyor 6 was one of several robotic lunar missions NASA sent to scout the moon before sending humans there. It took television pictures of the surface and learned about the composition of lunar soil. First Surveyor 6 launched from the surface and hopped to another position about 8 feet (2 meters) away. Next, Surveyor 6 took pictures of its original landing site.

news.title: NASA wants you to 'shine bright' today for Voyager 1's light-day milestone. Here's how
paras: The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov. 17), the day before Voyager 1 gets one light-day from Earth .

And that's a big milestone: One light-day is the distance light travels in a day — about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency. To celebrate the spacecraft, participants can use a flashlight, phone, bike light or other portable light source to send the signal skyward.
